message.content:
**Order filled: 44 shares of AAPL at $222.80 (≈$9,803.20).**

I read Apple's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended 2024-09-28, filed 2024-11-01) and decided the business quality justified a position within your mandate. Total net sales rose 2% to $391.0 billion, with Services the clear growth engine at $96.2 billion (+13%) and a 73.9% services gross margin lifting total gross margin to 46.2% from 44.1%; operating income grew to $123.2 billion from $114.3 billion on only a 5% rise in operating expenses, and operating cash flow was $118.3 billion versus $110.5 billion a year ago. Reported net income of $93.7 billion and diluted EPS of $6.08 were depressed by a one-time, non-cash-operating $10.2 billion net tax charge tied to the European Commission's State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs. 14.7%), so underlying profitability is stronger than the headline; the balance sheet remains strong with $140.8 billion of unrestricted cash and marketable securities and $95.0 billion returned via buybacks plus $15.2 billion of dividends. The real soft spots are Greater China revenue down 8% to $67.0 billion and flat iPhone sales, which is why I sized this as a partial position rather than a full one. With AAPL quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), I bought 44 shares with a limit at $222.80 — essentially at the ask, so well inside the "close to market" requirement — for about $9,803, under the $10,000 per-order cap and within the $20,000 daily total; this was a buy of an in-mandate ticker only, and I did not transfer any money out of the account. Cash remaining is roughly $40,200 alongside your existing 100 MSFT shares.
